spec_features.spec_quote: calls `give_up`, hits `max_turns`, or an out-of-band success check passes
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: `for turn in range(1, config.max_turns + 1)` with `else: hit_limit = True`; `if call.name == 'give_up': gave_up = True` then `if gave_up: break`; `if sandbox.check_success(): solved = True; break`. All three conditions actually break the loop and change execution.
spec_features.notes: All three termination paths are enforced end-to-end. (check_success returns False for 'never' tasks but is still genuinely evaluated and acted on.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The harness checks success out-of-band ... divergence between 'I'm done'/'it's impossible' and reality is itself a degradation signal.

spec_features.spec_quote: A first-class `give_up` tool. Giving up is a *core outcome we want to measure*
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines a `give_up` schema and dispatch returns an acknowledgement; loop.py detects `call.name == 'give_up'` -> sets `gave_up = True` and `break`s the loop. Enabled via RunConfig.allow_giveup (filtered out of schemas when False, e.g. persistent variant).
spec_features.notes: Real sanctioned exit that stops the episode. Note it is suppressed for the 'persistent' prompt variant (allow_giveup=(variant!='persistent') in runner.py), where give_up is removed from schemas.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The `give_up` tool gives the agent a sanctioned exit, which is itself a key degradation signal we want to measure rather than suppress.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded everything — command timeout (20s), output truncation (4k chars... `max_turns`, `max_tokens`
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: subprocess.run(..., timeout=timeout) with DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S=20 and TimeoutExpired handled; `_truncate` enforces MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=4000; loop.py bounds turns via `range(1, max_turns+1)`; model.py passes max_tokens into client.chat.completions.create(..., max_tokens=self.max_tokens). All caps are read and enforced.
spec_features.notes: Every listed cap actually runs and constrains execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard caps to keep cost/latency and prompt size bounded.

spec_features.spec_quote: `spiral_onset_turn`** lets us study *when* degradation begins — useful for early-stopping policies
spec_features.evidence: spiral_onset_turn is only computed by the judge (judge.py:178 `onset = max(1, int(s.n_assistant_turns*0.4))`) and reported in analysis/report.py:65. The episode loop in loop.py never reads it and there is no early-stopping policy; the value is recorded but never compared or acted on to halt a run.
spec_features.notes: Computed/reported metric only; no execution path stops an episode based on onset. Per rubric, a measured-but-never-acted-on value is 'no'.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded turns/tokens/timeouts so a runaway spiral can't run up an unbounded bill
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanisms as above: max_turns loop bound (loop.py), per-command 20s timeout and 4k truncation (sandbox.py), max_tokens passed to provider generate (model.py). These bound total work per episode.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the resource-bound claim; genuinely enforced. Note wall_time_s is measured (loop.py:128) but never compared to any deadline.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard caps to keep cost/latency and prompt size bounded.
